title: Customer capacity onboarding walkthrough (compact)
content:
Purpose:
Short walkthrough for onboarding a new dedicated customer contract into the reservation system. Lightweight, compact reference for infra on-call, solutions, and customer success during first 90 days.

Current fleet snapshot (global):
- Total GPUs (effective): 7,200 A100-equivalent (normalized).
- Regional capacity pools: us-west: 2,950 | us-east: 2,200 | eu-central: 1,250 | ap-south: 800
- Current dedicated reservations committed: 2,400 GPUs (33% of fleet) across all regions.
- Utilization moving-average (30d) on dedicated pools: 68%

Core assumptions and definitions (brief):
- Committed GPUs: guaranteed slabs in a regional pool for a contract (can be soft-pinned across AZs).
- Burst capacity: short-term extra capacity allowed up to X% of committed for N minutes subject to global fairshare.
- Effective GPU: normalized using perf-index table (A100x1.0, H100x1.2, L4x0.35).
- Buffer (operational slack): default 12% of regional pool reserved for autoscaling/backfills.

Onboarding checklist (operational steps) — minimal runbook: 
1) Intake & verification (SRE + Solutions): verify contract SLA windows, region affinity, and allowed burst. (JIRA-INFRA-2481)
2) Map contract to regional profile: decide primary region, fallback region(s), latency SLOs.
3) Create reservation slab in slot-allocator: record commit start/end, per-hour entitlement, and preemption policy.
4) Allocate buffer and liquid burst: default burst cap = min(20% of commit, 50 GPUs).
5) Update routing policy: customer routing tier and failure-fallback chain for model variants.
6) Smoke test with synthetic workload (10k tokens/min for 30 min) and validate tail latency < target.
7) Telemetry hooks: enable token-level metering, per-route tracing, and cost alerts (Console: tenant/<id>/billing).
8) Customer kickoff: share onboarding runbook + escalation path.

Compact allocation example (text table):
Contract | Commit GPUs | Region | Burst cap | Buffer reserved | Start | End | Notes
Alpha-Co | 120 GPUs | us-west | 24 GPU (20%) | 18 GPU (15%) | 2026-07-15 | 2027-07-14 | steady daytime traffic, prefer west
Beta-Apps | 480 GPUs | eu-central | 48 GPU (10%) | 60 GPU (12%) | 2026-06-01 | 2027-05-31 | bursty nightly batch windows
Gamma-Edge | 24 GPUs | ap-south | 12 GPU (50%) | 3 GPU (12.5%) | 2026-07-01 | 2026-12-31 | pilot; tight latency SLAs

Allocation logic notes (operational heuristics):
- Commit-to-pool mapping: allocate slabs from the smallest-suitable AZ group to reduce fragmentation.
- Fairshare enforcement: when global contention > 85% utilized, scale burst tolerance down by linear factor to 0 at 95% global utilization.
- Backfill policy: ephemeral workloads use backfill slots; these are preemptible and tagged as PREMPT-BACKFILL in the allocator.
- Sizing sanity check: require minimum 20% headroom from expected 90th percentile load to commit level. If headroom < 20% suggest revising commit.

Quick formulas (for spreadsheets):
- Effective committed GPU-hours per month = committed_GPUs * 24 * days_in_month * perf_index
- Expected monthly tokens = GPU-hours * tokens_per_hour_estimate (team to provide)
- Amortized cost per token = (monthly_commit_cost + burst_buffer_cost) / expected_monthly_tokens

Operational caveats & open questions (notes-to-self style):
- Q1: Should we default burst cap as a percentage or absolute GPU count? Current leaning: percentage for large contracts, absolute for small pilots.
- Q2: How to account for regional migration mid-contract (customer requests region move)? Need change window & cool-down (proposal: 14d notice, 7d drain).
- Q3: When multiple contracts have correlated peak windows (same timezone), how aggressive should cross-contract burst throttling be? Need simulation.

Short simulation excerpt (1-paragraph):
Ran a 72-hr sim with synthetic diurnal traffic for 20 customers. With default 12% buffer and 15% average burst, tail latency stayed within SLO for 87% of customers; top 2 high-burst tenants exceeded 95th latency at global utilization > 88%. Action: add dynamic per-contract burst telemetry and auto-shrink burst on global utilization alarms.

Rollout & timeline (practical):
- Week 0: config templates + slot-allocator schema updates (PR #67).
- Week 1: onboard 2 pilot contracts (Alpha-Co, Gamma-Edge) with manual monitoring and SRE rota.
- Week 3: adjust defaults based on pilot telemetry and sign off for broader onboarding.

Quick links & references:
- Slot allocator repo PR: github.com/redwood-inference/slot-allocator/pull/67
- Tests & sim harness: github.com/redwood-inference/capacity-sims/tree/pilot-2026
- Related Confluence: CONFLUENCE-9876 (reservation design notes)

Action items (who/what/when):
- Lucas: finalize slot-allocator change set and merge (due 2026-07-09).
- María: write the smoke test harness for burst behavior (due 2026-07-11).
- Aisha (me): draft customer-facing onboarding email/template (due 2026-07-12).

Version history / small audit trail:

- 2026-07-09: added sim excerpt + action items (Lucas)
- 2026-07-12: minor edits, clarified buffer policy (María)

Unresolved / parking lot:
- Integration with pricing engine for amortized cost per token (blocked on pricing API v2).
- Formal SLA template for cross-region failover periods.

If you're reading this during an on-call incident: look at the top section for the quick map, and the table to see hot contracts. For urgent questions ping #infra-reservations and tag @oncall-sre.
